newsitem.title: USA: Anaheim, Calif., voters OK tax for Disney expansion.
newsitem.headline: Anaheim, Calif., voters OK tax for Disney expansion.

text.p: Anaheim voters approved a local tax measure that will help fund projects linked to Walt Disney Co's $1.4 billion expansion of its Disneyland resort, election officials said on Wednesday.
Measure B reaffirmed a two percent increase in the local bed tax, which the city council approved in January 1995 without going to local voters.
Measure B, which required a simple majority to pass, received 74 percent support, election officials said.
The tax revenues will help to cover $546 million of proposed improvements as part of the Disney project.

Last month, the Anaheim city council approved the development plan for the Disney project as well as a financial agreement that would provide $546 million for infrastructure improvements to the area around the proposed theme park and for the city's convention facilities.

As part of the $546 million in improvements, $395 million of revenue bonds will be sold. City officials said state and federal grants and hotel and bed tax revenues would back the $546 million of proposed improvements. The city had held off on issuing the bonds until after the Nov 5 election on Measure B.
Following the vote, Anaheim spokesman Bret Colson said, "the next thing we have to do is sell $395 million of bonds, and then we're ready to start building the project."
